title: IN PHOTOS | Brewers' championship rally
summary: Fans gather in Milwaukee on Friday for the Brewers' championship parade and celebration after the Major League Baseball team won its first World Series in the franchise's 57-year history.

image.caption: This series of photos shows Brewers' William Contreras, the World Series MVP, holding up the Commissioner's Trophy as well as fans during a parade and rally in Milwaukee on Friday. (Nam Huh/The Associated Press, Angela Peterson/USA TODAY NETWORK/Imagn Images/Reuters, Matt Marton-Imagn Images/Reuters

blocks.text: Fans gather in Milwaukee on Friday for the Brewers' championship parade and celebration after the Major League Baseball team won its first World Series in the franchise's 57-year history.
Brewers fans gather in Milwaukee to celebrate franchise's 1st World Series title
The Milwaukee Brewers clinched their first-ever World Series on Wednesday, after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 5.
Here are the best moments from the Major League Baseball team's championship parade and rally in Milwaukee on Friday.
Brewers fans line up for the parade route in front of the Pfister hotel in downtown Milwaukee.
Fans arrive for the celebration at Henry Maier Festival Park.
A fan wears a foam cheese wedge known as a "Cheesehead."
This Brew Crew fan came to the rally wearing a 1982 American League Champions helmet.
And this animation gif shows William Contreras, the World Series MVP, holding up the Commissioner's Trophy; Christian Yelich in the foreground; and Aaron Ashby with the trophy, during the rally.
Smoke and streamers go off on stage.
